title: Best Apps for Crohn's Disease: Symptoms to Biologics
summary: See why Aidy is the best overall Crohn's app among six options, plus the best alternatives for wearables, Android access, and customization.
body_markdown:
**Quick answer:** Among the six apps reviewed here, Aidy offers the best overall combination of features for Crohn's disease. It brings symptom, stool, and meal tracking together with ordinary medications, detailed biologic schedules, injection-site rotation, post-dose check-ins, modified[Harvey-Bradshaw Index trends](https://aidyhq.com/learn/crohns-harvey-bradshaw-index-what-your-hbi-means) , and doctor-ready reports in one iPhone app that is free to download ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/aidy-manage-crohns-colitis/id6747647744) ). Flarity is the better fit for wearable inputs, MyGut for free iPhone and Android access, and Bearable for broader chronic-illness customization.


This is a feature-based verdict, not evidence that one app improves Crohn's outcomes more than another. A systematic review found that IBD apps commonly support symptom monitoring and medication adherence, but feature sets vary considerably ([Middle East Journal of Digestive Diseases](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11725021/) ). Features and availability were checked on August 26, 2026.


## Crohn's App Comparison at a Glance


App Best fit Main tradeoff


Aidy Best overall combination for Crohn's symptoms, medications, biologics, scores, and reports Currently iPhone only


Flarity Wearable signals and shareable clinical reports Flare warning is a product prediction, not a diagnosis


Chronicare Daily IBD tracking with community Less public detail about Crohn's scores and biologic workflows


MyGut Free, nonprofit-led tracking on iPhone and Android No detailed biologic workflow listed


My IBD Care Education and whole-person support Linked-care functions depend on participating UK services


Bearable Custom tracking across multiple chronic conditions Crohn's-specific fields require more setup


We compared the apps across daily Crohn's tracking, medication and biologic support, Crohn's-specific scores, report sharing, platform access, and each product's clearest specialty. "Best overall" means the broadest useful combination of those publicly documented features, while the alternatives may be better for a narrower priority.


## Choose the Job Before You Choose the App


A Crohn's disease symptom tracker app should make repeated information easier to retrieve. Useful fields may include[bowel frequency and form](https://aidyhq.com/learn/what-to-track-with-crohns-building-a-symptom-diary-that-actually-helps) , abdominal pain, fatigue, meals, medication adherence, and free-text context. During diagnosis and reassessment, clinicians may also use[blood tests, stool tests, endoscopy, and imaging](https://aidyhq.com/learn/how-crohns-disease-is-diagnosed-every-test-explained) , so a diary represents one part of the clinical picture ([NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/crohns-disease/diagnosis) ).


Start with the decision you are trying to support. A person beginning an injected biologic may prioritize dose dates, reminders, injection sites, and post-dose notes. Someone with[several chronic conditions](https://aidyhq.com/learn/chronic-illness-trackers-for-crohns-10-apps-compared) may prefer customizable symptoms and wearable data. A newly diagnosed user may value guided education and questionnaires. App-store research has also found meaningful differences in engagement and quality among IBD apps, which makes a short real-world trial more useful than choosing by screenshots alone ([International Journal of Medical Informatics](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37857167/) ).


## Six Crohn's Apps Compared by Use Case


**Aidy** is the broadest fit for Crohn's users who want symptoms, stools, meals, ordinary medications, and biologics in one record. Its current listing describes configurable[induction and maintenance schedules](https://aidyhq.com/learn/what-to-track-during-induction-and-maintenance-treatment) , dose reminders, injection-site rotation, post-dose check-ins, modified Harvey-Bradshaw Index trends, and doctor-ready reports. It is currently an iPhone app and is free to download ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/aidy-manage-crohns-colitis/id6747647744) ).


**Flarity** is the wearable-focused option. Its official feature page lists heart-rate variability, sleep and activity inputs, Harvey-Bradshaw Index reporting, medication adherence, laboratory capture, on-device processing, and a shareable clinical report. Its flare-warning output is a developer claim and should be interpreted within the evidence supplied for that specific model ([Flarity](https://getflarity.com/) ).


**Chronicare** combines IBD tracking with community. Its site describes logging for symptoms, meals, bowel movements, and medications, plus reports and peer discussion. That combination may suit someone who wants social support beside a daily diary ([Chronicare](https://chronicare.io/) ).


**MyGut** is a free nonprofit option from Crohn's and Colitis Canada. It covers pain, bowel movements, urgency, sleep, stress, flare check-ins, quality-of-life questionnaires, and a history view. The organization says it is available on iOS and Android without fees or ads ([Crohn's and Colitis Canada](https://crohnsandcolitis.ca/Support-for-You/MyGut) ).


**My IBD Care** puts more emphasis on clinician-developed education and whole-person support. Its public materials describe symptom, medication, appointment, mood, sleep, and stress tracking, along with courses and an AI guide. Hospital-linked functions currently depend on participating UK services, although the self-service app is available more broadly ([Ampersand Health](https://ampersandhealth.co.uk/myibdcare/) ).


**Bearable** is a general chronic-illness tracker. It supports customizable symptoms, medication, sleep, energy, mood, nutrition, wearable data, and correlation reports. This flexibility can help people managing Crohn's alongside other conditions, but Crohn's-specific fields require more setup ([Bearable](https://bearable.app/) ).


## Biologic Tracking and Crohn's Scores Need Context


A Crohn's biologic reminder app should preserve the prescribed interval, actual administration date, route, and any note you want to discuss later. It should never calculate a new dosing plan. Aidy's listing is unusually specific about induction and maintenance phases, route or interval changes, site rotation, and check-ins after injections or infusions ([Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/aidy-manage-crohns-colitis/id6747647744) ). Flarity and My IBD Care describe medication adherence, while MyGut and Chronicare provide broader medication records.


The Harvey-Bradshaw Index is a structured Crohn's activity measure built mainly from symptoms and clinical observations; recent research also shows that translating another patient-reported score into HBI carries uncertainty ([Inflammatory Bowel Diseases](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12342735/) ). The American Gastroenterological Association recommends[combining symptoms with biomarkers](https://aidyhq.com/learn/treat-to-target-ibd-what-patients-need-to-know) in several Crohn's monitoring situations rather than relying on symptoms alone ([Gastroenterology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37981354/) ). An app score can organize a trend for discussion, while biomarkers, imaging, and endoscopy answer different questions.


## A Practical Selection Standard


The strongest app is the one you can use consistently and export clearly. Before settling on one, test how quickly you can record a difficult day, whether medication history remains understandable after a schedule change, and whether the report distinguishes raw entries from predictions. Review platform access, subscription boundaries, privacy disclosures, account deletion, and data export directly in the current listing.


Research supports a measured view of digital IBD tools. A 2025 umbrella review found that digital health interventions may assist treatment adherence and reduce some hospital use, while the reviewed evidence did not show a direct improvement in maintaining clinical remission ([The Lancet Digital Health](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40374487/) ). For biologic-centered Crohn's tracking, Aidy covers the widest set of relevant jobs in this group. Flarity has the clearest wearable emphasis, Chronicare adds community, MyGut offers nonprofit-led tracking, My IBD Care emphasizes education, and Bearable provides broad customization. Those distinctions provide a more durable basis for choosing than a single overall ranking.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best app for tracking Crohn's disease?


Aidy is the best overall option among the apps reviewed here for someone who wants Crohn's symptoms, stools, meals, medications, biologic schedules, modified HBI trends, and doctor reports in one place. MyGut is a stronger choice when Android access is essential, while Flarity is more specialized for wearable data.


### Can a Crohn's app tell whether I am having a flare?


No app log, score, or prediction can confirm intestinal inflammation by itself. Symptom trends can help describe a change, but clinicians may also use biomarkers, imaging, endoscopy, and other assessment ([American Gastroenterological Association](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37981354/) ). Contact your care team about severe, rapidly worsening, or concerning symptoms rather than waiting for an app result.


### What should I track for a gastroenterology appointment?


Useful records often include bowel frequency and form, pain, fatigue, meals, medication adherence, biologic dose dates, and brief notes about unusual events. A short, consistent record that your clinician can review is usually more useful than a complicated diary you cannot maintain.
